analysis.title: Global Markets Outlook 2027 (Macro Markets Outlook 2027: Growing Pains)
key_insights: GS describes a maturing market cycle in its 2027 outlook, with leadership passing between asset classes and regions (slides titled 'A Maturing Market Cycle' and 'Passing—or Dropping—the Baton').

Global equities tend to do well when earnings growth is good, but the second derivative (change in the growth rate) matters. The chart compares MSCI AC World 12m returns vs US 10-year bonds against equity carry (dividend yield plus ex-post 12m EPS growth).

Global equity valuations have already de-rated materially. GS reads this as markets pricing an earnings growth slowdown, so valuation drag has already been material (1-year change in NTM P/E vs 12m-ahead NTM EPS growth).
Bond-like equities can help diversify tech exposure. As in the Tech Bubble, the proportion of S&P 500 stocks with a negative beta has increased.
Bonds have reclaimed macro and hedging value. Stock-bond correlation is measured with ES and TY futures, and 10y bond total returns in 2026 are plotted against 2y1y sensitivity to oil prices.
The deck has sections on Europe and the UK (global shocks and local shifts), Asia's revaluing currencies, and a more cyclical dollar, with EPFR flow data cited for the dollar slide.
Equity has historically outperformed credit, especially during tech booms. The chart scales credit excess return to match equity volatility and measures equity excess return against T-bills.

Over the last 5 years, allocations to gold and other real assets have materially improved performance vs standard 60/40 portfolios (5-year rolling Sharpe ratio, 60/40 S&P 500/10y bonds vs 60/40 S&P 500/gold vs 60/40 with a real asset index).
Energy is framed as balancing risk and risk premium, and EM as offering resilience and diversification (two slides).
earnings_insights: Global equities tend to do well with good earnings growth, but the second derivative matters. Equity carry is defined as dividend yield plus ex-post 12m EPS growth, with a consensus-EPS-based variant. No specific EPS figures are given in the text.
risk_factors: An earnings growth slowdown, which the report says markets are already pricing through de-rated valuations.
Concentration in tech, which the report says can be diversified with bond-like equities.
charts_described: Chart: MSCI AC World 12m return vs US 10-year bonds against equity carry (dividend yield + ex-post 12m EPS growth), 1950 onward, y-axis from -75% to 75%.
Chart: 1-year change in NTM P/E vs 12m-ahead growth in NTM EPS, 1990 to 2025.
Chart: proportion of S&P 500 stocks with a negative beta, 1990 to 2025, on 3-month daily and 1-year weekly betas.
Chart: 5-year rolling Sharpe ratio of 60/40 S&P 500/US 10-year bonds vs 60/40 S&P 500/gold vs 60/40 S&P 500/real asset index, 1950 onward.
vol_and_positioning: The proportion of S&P 500 stocks with a negative beta has risen, similar to the Tech Bubble, measured on 3-month beta from daily returns and 1-year beta from weekly returns.
